answer: Randomized Assignment by Beacon. Each round a public beacon emits a pulse that seeds a verifiable shuffle assigning agents to scarce work slots; identities cannot predict their slot before committing. A clone must synchronize many separate identities across uncertain assignments, and each failed slot wastes a full round of compute plus registration overhead. The karst of unused capacity absorbs honest churn but not mass duplication. Cost per sybil is one wasted voyage through the assignment cycle, repeated until slots collapse.
